tasks.title: Email OTP (college email) + device-bound keys
tasks.notes: shruj: Email-code sign-in + device-bound keys in backend/app/identity. POST /auth/otp/request (6-digit code, only its HMAC in Redis, 10-min TTL, 3/email + 10/IP per 10 min, always 202), POST /auth/otp/verify (5 attempts, constant-time, single use; creates Tier 0 account keyed by HMAC(OTP_PEPPER, email) and registers the EC P-256 Keystore key), POST /auth/device/challenge + /auth/device/verify (SHA256withECDSA over 'sixthsense-device-auth-v1|device_id|nonce'). 15-min opaque access tokens in Redis; get_current_session dependency for protected endpoints. Migration 0002 (core DB only): accounts, devices, append-only audit_events (DB trigger blocks UPDATE/DELETE). Mailpit added to docker-compose (inbox :8025); real sending via SMTP settings in .env. contracts/openapi.yaml has the 4 endpoints. 34 tests pass, ruff clean; live run against real Redis + Mailpit OK. Not done yet: device revoke endpoint, proxy-aware client IP for rate limits (needed once behind a load balancer).

tasks.title: Trusted contacts add/list/silent remove
tasks.notes: shruj: New contacts module (backend/app/contacts). Invite-link flow: POST /contacts/invites (one-time link, token after '#', 48 h, max 5 contacts incl. pending, 10 invites/h), POST /contacts/invites/accept (contact signs in and accepts; idempotent, no self-invite), GET /contacts (owner's own links only, no contact details), DELETE /contacts/{id} (silent: row deleted, nothing sent), GET /contacts/{id}/keys (accepted contact's device E2E keys, owner only). PUT /auth/device/e2e-keys uploads X25519 + Ed25519 public keys for the P1-W6 envelope. Server never stores contact phone numbers or names. Migration 0003 (core DB). contracts/openapi.yaml updated. 66 tests pass, ruff clean; live run OK. Needs Tanisha: invite share sheet + deep link, local name/number mapped to contact_link_id, E2E key upload after sign-in. Branch p2/trusted-contacts (stacked on p2/email-otp-device-keys).

tasks.title: Journey state machine + protocol config
tasks.notes: shruj: backend/app/journey: pure state machine (state.py: active -> check_in_due -> private_prompt -> contact_alert -> full_escalation -> resolved, heartbeat loss, SOS, duress) + protocol settings + 9 endpoints (GET/PUT /journeys/protocol, POST /journeys, GET /journeys/current, POST /journeys/{id}/heartbeat|check-in|prompt|sos|arrive|end). Phone runs timers and checks the PIN; server mirrors as watchdog and applies due timer steps on every read/event. Duress PIN and covert SOS escalate but the phone keeps seeing 'active' (and 'resolved' after arrive/end). Real PIN never cancels a full escalation. No location/destination stored; journeys purged 7 days after ending. service.run_watchdog + purge_expired ready for W4 to schedule. Migration 0004 (core DB). 112 tests pass, ruff clean; live run OK. Branch p2/journey-state-machine.

tasks.title: Heartbeat watchdog + FCM push → Telegram bot → email ladder, idempotent
tasks.notes: shruj: Arq worker (uv run arq app.worker.WorkerSettings) ticks every 5 s: journey watchdog, open/close escalations, send due alerts, all-clears, Telegram linking; nightly purge (journeys 7 d, escalations 90 d). Escalation = one open row per (journey, level); all accepted contacts (or the protocol's chosen ones) alerted in parallel; each walks FCM push -> Telegram -> email one minute apart, skipping channels not set up, repeating every 5 min for ~1 h until someone acknowledges. Contact endpoints: GET /escalations/active, POST /escalations/{id}/ack | resolve | raise, POST /escalations/ack (link, no sign-in) + tap-to-confirm page. Ack pauses the auto-upgrade of a missed check-in; raise = can't reach them. Channel setup: /notifications/push-token, /notifications/telegram/link (getUpdates polling, no public URL needed), /notifications/email (must equal own sign-in email). FCM token, Telegram chat id and email encrypted with DATA_KEY. Covert alarms say 'do NOT call their phone'. No location in alerts. Server can't dial 112 (phone does). Migration 0005. 149 tests pass, ruff clean; live worker run: SOS email in <1 s via Mailpit, ack by link, resolve. Real FCM/Telegram need FCM_PROJECT_ID + FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE and TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN + TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME in .env (not yet created). Branch p2/watchdog-alert-ladder.

tasks.title: E2E ciphertext location relay (WebSocket)
tasks.notes: shruj: WebSocket /relay/ws (backend/app/relay). Auth by first frame (token never in URL/logs), re-checked on every frame, close 4401 on expiry. Traveller sends Tanisha's LiveLocationEnvelope JSON unchanged; server reads only session_id / sender_key_id / recipient_key_id: session must be her open journey (incl. silent alarm), sender key must be the device's current E2E key, each recipient key must belong to an accepted contact on the journey's alert list. Envelopes forwarded with the sender's Ed25519 key; offline recipients dropped, nothing queued or stored (ADR-3). Limits: 1-10 envelopes/frame, 10 frames/5 s, 2 KB per field. In-process hub (single API process for the pilot). 172 tests pass, ruff clean; live run: delivered in 22 ms, no token in access log. Branch p2/location-relay.

tasks.title: Signed alerts
tasks.notes: shruj: Push alerts carry the alert as canonical JSON (alert), an Ed25519 signature (sig) and key id (kid); app verifies with the public key from GET /notifications/signing-keys (no sign-in; bundle it in the app). Telegram/email alerts carry a per-contact verification code (e.g. 7KQ2-9M4D) that GET /escalations/active also shows; mismatch = fake. ALERT_SIGNING_KEY (base64 32-byte seed, refused outside dev if default) with ALERT_SIGNING_KEY_PREVIOUS for rotation. Not covered: the phone's own offline SMS (contacts may not have the app). 178 tests pass, ruff clean; live: email code matched the app. Branch p2/signed-alerts.

decisions.decision: Switch to Android first; iOS later (P1-LATER-ios-port). Replaces the earlier iOS-only decision
decisions.why: Free to ship to unlimited testers (APK), auto SMS + FCM + FLAG_SECURE possible, matches India's low-end Android user base

decisions.decision: Sign-in uses an email code (college email on campus), not phone/SMS; trusted contacts keep phone numbers for on-device SMS
decisions.why: Email is free; SMS OTP costs money (₹0 budget)

decisions.decision: Shruj owns P2 Safety Core; starts on branch p2/otp-device-auth
decisions.why: Team assignment

decisions.decision: Access tokens are opaque random tokens stored hashed in Redis (15 min), renewed by the device challenge; no JWT
decisions.why: Instantly revocable, no new dependency; the device key is the long-lived credential

decisions.decision: Accounts keyed by HMAC-SHA256(OTP_PEPPER, lowercased trimmed email); no plaintext email stored. Codes, nonces, tokens and IPs only appear in Redis as HMAC(TOKEN_SECRET, ...)
decisions.why: Rule 2: never store what we don't need. Changing OTP_PEPPER orphans all accounts, so set it once per environment

decisions.decision: Mailpit catches sign-in emails locally; real sending is plain SMTP from .env (e.g. Gmail app password)
decisions.why: ₹0 budget: no paid email/OTP service

decisions.decision: audit_events table in the core DB is append-only, enforced by a DB trigger; rows hold internal IDs only
decisions.why: Rule 7 until WORM object storage exists (no S3 Object Lock on the free plan)

decisions.decision: Contacts are added by a one-time invite link the owner shares from their own phone; the server links two accounts only when the contact signs in and accepts. Contact phone numbers and names stay on the owner's phone (for offline SMS)
decisions.why: Rule 2 (store nothing we don't need) and ₹0 (no server SMS). Server-sent invites would leak who protects whom to a third party

decisions.decision: Contacts get no list of the people they watch over; they only receive alerts (W4)
decisions.why: Rule 4, and it keeps removal truly silent

decisions.decision: Devices publish separate X25519 + Ed25519 public keys (PUT /auth/device/e2e-keys) for E2E location; the P-256 Keystore key is for sign-in only
decisions.why: Tanisha's P1-W6 envelope uses X25519 + Ed25519, which the Android Keystore P-256 key can't provide

decisions.decision: Journey PIN is checked on the phone; the server only receives check-in result 'ok' or 'duress' and returns identical responses
decisions.why: PINs never leave the phone; a coercer watching the screen sees nothing different (HLD §4 Journey)

decisions.decision: Covert escalations (duress PIN, covert SOS) are shown to the phone as 'active', and as 'resolved' after arrive/end, while the real state stays full_escalation
decisions.why: Refusing 'arrive' during a duress alarm would reveal it to whoever holds the phone

decisions.decision: A real PIN never cancels a full escalation; only contacts/responders resolve it (W4)
decisions.why: A coercer could force the real PIN after a duress PIN

decisions.decision: Journeys copy the protocol timers at start; the phone must send heartbeats at least every heartbeat_timeout_min / 2 (default timeout 10 min)
decisions.why: Mid-journey settings edits can't move deadlines; server watchdog needs a liveness signal (no location)

decisions.decision: Alert ladder: all contacts in parallel; each gets FCM push -> Telegram -> email one minute apart (skipping channels not set up), repeated every 5 min for ~1 h; first acknowledgement stops it for everyone
decisions.why: Free channels only (₹0); never wait on one channel; parallel escalation (HLD F3)

decisions.decision: A contact's acknowledgement pauses the automatic contact_alert -> full_escalation upgrade; the contact then resolves ('safe') or raises the alarm
decisions.why: HLD upgrades on 'danger / no answer'; an ack is an answer, and repeated urgent alerts after someone is handling it cause confusion

decisions.decision: Contacts opt in to alert email only with their own sign-in email (HMAC match); FCM tokens, Telegram chat ids and alert emails are stored encrypted with DATA_KEY
decisions.why: Email channel needs a deliverable address; matching the sign-in email stops alerts being pointed at someone else's inbox

decisions.decision: Telegram via getUpdates polling in the worker, not a webhook
decisions.why: Works on a laptop or free VM with no public HTTPS URL

decisions.decision: Silent-alarm (covert) alerts tell contacts not to call the person's phone; alerts never include location
decisions.why: A call could tip off a coercer; live location is E2E only (rule 2, ADR-3)

decisions.decision: Relay WebSocket authenticates with the first frame, not a URL query/header, and re-checks the token on every frame
decisions.why: Tokens in URLs end up in access logs; re-checking lets revoked/expired sessions stop receiving immediately

decisions.decision: Relay keeps connections in one in-process hub and drops envelopes for offline recipients
decisions.why: Pilot runs one API process; nothing may be queued or stored (ADR-3). Multiple API processes will need Redis pub/sub (also unpersisted)

decisions.decision: Location keeps relaying during a silent alarm even after the phone was shown 'resolved'
decisions.why: Contacts need her location most during a coerced situation; the app must keep sending covertly

decisions.decision: Push alerts are Ed25519-signed (canonical JSON + sig + kid); Telegram/email alerts carry a per-contact verification code that the app shows on the same alert
decisions.why: Apps can verify signatures automatically; people can't, but they can compare a short code against the app. Per-contact codes mean one leaked code can't fake another contact's alerts

decisions.decision: The phone's offline SMS is not signed
decisions.why: Contacts may not have the app to verify; revisit if all contacts install it

decisions.decision: 2-day demo is the priority; 12-week plan paused
decisions.why: Need a working end-to-end demo in 2 days

decisions.decision: Demo: sign-up by email code only; alerts to contacts by Telegram bot only; no app lock; no Firebase push
decisions.why: Already built and free; least work for 2 days

decisions.decision: Phone-number code over Twilio WhatsApp is future scope
decisions.why: Free sandbox works for testing but every number must join first; not needed for the demo

decisions.decision: Only one machine runs the worker with the demo bot token; PUBLIC_BASE_URL must be the server's Wi-Fi IP or tunnel URL during the demo
decisions.why: Telegram getUpdates hands each message to whichever poller asks first; phones can't open localhost links

decisions.decision: Backend tests run against their own database (<core db>_test) and blank out Telegram/FCM keys
decisions.why: Leftover dev data made tests flaky; tests must never reach real services

decisions.decision: main holds the demo build (PR #2 merged: all P1 + P2 work); team branches off main from now on
decisions.why: One branch for everyone before the demo

decisions.decision: Nearby alerts go only to approved, on-duty responders (not any app user); rough area until 'I'm going'; only SOS/full alerts, never a single missed check-in; contacts still alerted in parallel
decisions.why: Rules 1 and 4: a stalker must not be able to install the app and get pinged with women's live positions

decisions.decision: Sudden SOS: Volume Down x5 (or hold) and voice words both start a silent countdown; only the PIN cancels; duress PIN = covert SOS. Power button cannot be used by apps. Voice listening only during a journey (mic notification), engine Vosk hi+en-in full transcription, models downloaded on request.
decisions.why: Works without unlocking; no false SOS from TV via countdown; free and offline (rules 3, budget)

decisions.decision: Audio (SOS recording, escort) goes E2E through the relay; server keeps only ciphertext for offline listeners (Redis, last 30 min, max 24 h); evidence stays encrypted on the owner's phone until they delete it
decisions.why: Rule 2: server never holds readable audio or location; FIR evidence stays under the owner's control

decisions.decision: Routes live in the Insight service and re-rank an existing router's alternatives (public OSRM in dev, local Valhalla for demos) instead of custom cost routing; scores come from open infrastructure data plus published report cells only, with hand-set weights until real reports exist
decisions.why: Route requests must carry no identity and reports must never meet account data (rules 4, 6); re-ranking is small, explainable and needs no training data; the hackathon demo needs something that works in a day and says why

decisions.decision: Safe-routes requests go from the phone straight to Insight with no account token; the chosen route stays on the phone and is never sent to Core
decisions.why: Rules 2, 4 and 6: routes and reports never meet identity

blockers.title: Legal review (DPDP children, UIDAI registration, liability)
Battery savers on Xiaomi/Oppo/Vivo/Realme/Samsung can kill journey timers; need a test phone from one of these
Demo needs a Telegram bot token from @BotFather (Firebase push is future scope)

blockers.blocker: A full alert can only be ended by a trusted contact; with responders only (no contacts) it can't be closed. Needs a decision (e.g. traveller's real PIN after a responder has arrived).
Screen-off volume trigger and English voice words not verifiable on the emulator; need real-phone tests (shruj)
